🚀 AstroNex – Innovating Beyond Earth

We are AstroNex, a technology-driven team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Karachi, Pakistan.

Our team brings together interests in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Software Engineering, Web Development, Data Science, and Space Technology. We are passionate about transforming real-world challenges into meaningful, innovative solutions using technology and scientific thinking.
summary:
AgroUs (AgroMind AI) is an open-source, explainable crop-rotation decision support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Challenge: Field Shift) by team AstraAgent. Designed to address agricultural resilience, escalating water scarcity, and soil degradation, AgroUs empowers smallholder farmers and agronomists to evaluate sustainable multi-year crop rotations tailored to local microclimates. 

By fusing seven NASA Earth-observation datasets—including NASA POWER agroclimatology, MODIS NDVI vegetation cycles, SMAP root-zone soil moisture, GRACE groundwater anomalies, and SRTM elevation—with farmer inputs, local soil observations, and field photos, AgroUs generates resilient, water-conscious rotation strategies with zero external cloud AI dependencies. It models economic gross margins, FAO salinity and water thresholds, and future climate robustness entirely locally and offline. Crucially, AgroUs pairs automated intelligence with human-in-the-loop expert review, bridging spaceborne science and on-the-ground farming to protect food security and farmer livelihoods.
details:
Overview & How It Works

AgroUs (AgroMind AI) is a local, explainable crop rotation decision support system that converts NASA Earth Observation data into actionable, field-level agricultural guidance.

The system follows a modular pipeline:

1. Farmer Input & Validation: A 5-step wizard captures field boundaries, current crops, irrigation types, and soil observations. Inputs are validated against administrative boundaries and an offline gazetteer of 680 places.

2. Earth Observation Agent: Integrates NASA POWER meteorological data, MODIS Terra NDVI, SMAP soil moisture, GRACE groundwater storage anomalies, MODIS Land Surface Temperature, and SRTM elevation data. All data is cached locally for offline access.

3. AgroVision Agent: Analyzes field photographs of soil and leaves using lighting correction, color-based symptom detection, and a locally embedded MobileNetV2 crop disease diagnostic model.

4. Soil & Crop Rules Engine: Combines soil texture, laboratory ECe salinity measurements, satellite bare-month validation, and FAO-29/56 agronomic thresholds.

5. Multi-Year Rotation Strategy: Generates and evaluates alternative crop rotation sequences, including Baseline, Legume-Inclusive, Water-Conscious, and Forage strategies over 2–3 years. Calculates gross margins, water savings, and stress resilience.

6. Scientific Validation & Audit: Tags every recommendation with its data source, confidence level, and scientific evidence to prevent unsupported claims.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

- Resilient Agriculture: Helps farmers break monoculture cycles, restore soil health, and reduce yield losses caused by changing climate conditions.

- Water Conservation: Uses satellite soil moisture and meteorological trends to identify water stress and recommend rotations that reduce irrigation demand.

- Privacy & Accessibility: Operates locally and offline without requiring cloud computing, expensive subscriptions, or sharing farmers' location data.

- Human-in-the-Loop: Provides an Agronomist Expert Review portal where local experts validate and approve regional sowing calendars and crop recommendations.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software

  • Programming Languages: Python 3.10+, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3
  • Earth Observation & Geospatial: NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS (WMS and colormap decoders), geoBoundaries (PAK ADM1–3)
  • Machine Learning & Computer Vision: PyTorch, ONNX, MobileNetV2, NumPy, Pillow, OpenCV
  • Backend & Storage: FastAPI, Starlette, SQLite with automated startup backups
  • Frontend & Visualization: Vanilla JavaScript, Leaflet.js, Canvas charts, PDF generation
  • Containerization: Docker and Docker Compose, locally bound to 127.0.0.1

Creativity & Special Considerations

- Zero Cloud Hallucination: Uses transparent, deterministic multi-agent rules based on FAO standards and NASA satellite measurements rather than relying on generic conversational AI.

- Offline-First Architecture: Uses pre-cached spatial grids and lightweight local vision models for deployment in remote agricultural areas with limited connectivity.

- Dual-Language Accessibility: Supports Urdu and English summaries, visual risk indicators, and text-to-speech accessibility features.
